title: Out of Life

location.name: Window Frame Tower, Hometown Skyline (HOME district, Baltimere)
location.kind: high-rise apartment bedroom with an iron fire escape outside the window
location.real_analog: a 12-14 story pre-war brick apartment tower in Baltimore's Mount Vernon, iron fire escapes bolted under the bedroom windows
near: open air / clouds below the window

situation: In a plain, dim high-rise bedroom the POET (black t-shirt) reads the poem aloud to the EX, who sits outside on the fire escape, back to him, vaping, while a TV cycles images of the world's chaos. Vape haze fills the room inside and out; he moves toward the window but the EX recedes, then falls off the fire escape into darkness and he falls after through clouds into black. Mid-fall (title card) he crashes into an old-time vintage party, chases the EX through the slow-motion crowd but the EX keeps vanishing, then trips through a hole in the floor into pure blackness.
time_of_day: evening into night (inferred: 'room dim'; spine SH010 places the fire escape at dusk)
weather_light: dim interior, TV flicker, thick vape haze blurring vision; then cloud and total black; the party is warm with euphoric light leaks

set_pieces.what_happens: POET stumbles through a hole in the party floor and keeps falling into pure blackness.
lines: as I stumble / on my own words,
set_pieces.camera: low floor-level angle on his feet catching the edge, then overhead as he drops away into black

arrival.from_previous: Film opens here: 'Open on plain bedroom, high rise, room dim.' No previous place.

departure.to_next: He trips through a hole in the party floor and falls into pure blackness, where Flashing Lights finds him falling or floating.

encoding: A high window with a fire escape is a built-in exit that is also a ledge: the 'way out' the poem looks for is literally hanging off the bedroom, and the EX is already out on it. The fall from the tower turns the escape route into the poem's thesis - leaving is falling - and every later place (party, void, flashback) is reached by dropping through a floor. Inferred: the high floor is what makes the fall long enough to pass through a whole culture of escapism.
